headline: AI tool detects inflated mechanic quotes running 100% on your laptop, ensures privacy
summary: Wrenchwise analyzes repair estimates against fair-price data, flagging inflated items and explaining them in plain English, all while keeping your data private by running entirely on-device.
details: Wrenchwise is a new web app designed to help car owners identify inflated repair estimates. It analyzes any pasted repair bill against fair-price data, flagging suspicious line items and explaining them in plain English. Crucially, its AI runs entirely on your device, ensuring complete privacy.

The single-file web app allows users to paste an estimate, select their region, and receive an instant analysis. A built-in sample estimate demonstrates how it catches realistically padded bills in seconds, highlighting potential overcharges.

The architecture uses two layers: curated PRICE_PACKS for regional fair-price data (e.g., 22 common jobs for India, 14 for the US) and an on-device AI model (Google's Gemma 2B) for explanations. The price ranges are indicative baselines compiled from published service-price sources.

Running the AI model locally keeps costs low, enabling a $2 per-quote pricing model with zero marginal cost for the developer. This on-device approach also ensures user privacy, as sensitive data like VINs and phone numbers never leave the user's machine. It also avoids vendor lock-in and allows for niche-specific data interpretation.

Beyond individual car owners, who can save significant amounts (e.g., ₹4,450 on a sample bill), the tool also presents a B2B opportunity. Independent garages could white-label a 'verified fair quote' badge to build trust with new customers.

headline_marked: [[Samsung Galaxy Glasses leak reveals]] designs, specs, and 41g weight
headline: Samsung Galaxy Glasses leak reveals designs, specs, and 41g weight
summary: The leak details a 41-gram weight, making them lighter than Meta Ray-Bans, and hints at diverse frame designs from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker.
details: Samsung's Android XR-powered Galaxy Glasses are expected later this year, with a new leak from SammyGuru detailing designs and specs. They are reportedly lighter than Meta Ray-Ban Gen 3, weighing around 41 grams with standard lenses.
The glasses are said to feature a Qualcomm Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chipset, 2GB RAM, and 64GB storage. A 12MP camera capable of 3K video at 30fps is also expected.
Similar to other smart glasses, they will include open-ear speakers and built-in microphones for calls and music. The battery life is reportedly up to 72 hours when used with the charging case.

A significant part of the leak highlights the variety of frame designs. Gentle Monster is expected to offer six styles with up to 16 variants, including square, round, cat-eye, and oval shapes in various colors.
Warby Parker will reportedly introduce three designs: Alden, Reid, and Wren. These will come in colors like Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black, with options for clear or sunglass lenses.

The Galaxy Glasses are rumored for a November launch, initially in South Korea and the U.S. Pricing remains unknown, but they are expected to be sold via eyewear brands' websites and Samsung Experience Stores.
